---
description: "Use when creating or updating README.md files. Covers README structure, useful project information, examples, and accuracy."
name: "README Guidelines"
applyTo: "**/README.md"
---
# README Guidelines

- Start with the project name and a concise overview explaining what it does, who it is for, and the problem it solves.
- Add a short feature summary when it helps readers quickly assess the project.
- Include relevant status badges only when they are maintained and useful.
- Document prerequisites and supported platforms or versions.
- Provide installation instructions and a quick-start example that readers can copy and run. Verify commands, parameters, and expected behavior against the project.
- Link to detailed documentation rather than duplicating it. Add configuration, troubleshooting, or limitations when they are important to getting started.
- For developer-facing projects, explain how to build, test, and contribute; include license information or a link when available.
- Keep the document scannable with descriptive headings, concise prose, and fenced code blocks with the appropriate language.
- Prefer useful, project-specific information over boilerplate. Do not add sections that do not apply, claim unsupported capabilities, or include unverified examples.
